rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance annual allowable rent increase (1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027)
rules.requirement: If you live in a rent-controlled unit in San Francisco, your landlord's annual rent increase from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 cannot be more than 1.6% of your base rent. For example, a $2,000 base rent can go up by no more than $32.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units under the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. Neither member says which units are covered. The city's just-cause page (D079, another category) says the rent increase limits do not apply to new units that first got a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979, to tenancies where Costa-Hawkins allows rent increases, or to some units whose rent another government agency regulates.
rules.exemptions: Units first certificated for occupancy after June 13, 1979; tenancies where Costa-Hawkins allows rent increases; some units whose rent another government agency regulates (from D079 context).
rules.reason: Two official Rent Board pages give the same 1.6% allowable increase under S.F. Admin. Code § 37.3(a)(1), so they are merged. The effective date is left null because March 1, 2026 is only this year's adjustment date, and neither member gives the ordinance's original start date.
